entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17702"/><div sID="gen35789" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv17702"/><hi type="bold">3. long on the earth--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Exod.20.12">Ex 20:12</reference>, "long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee," which Paul adapts to Gospel times, by taking away the local and limited reference peculiar to the Jews in Canaan. The godly are equally blessed in every land, as the Jews were in the land which God gave them. This promise is always fulfilled, either literally, or by the substitution of a higher blessing, namely, one spiritual and eternal (<reference osisRef="Job.5.26">Job 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.10.27">Pr 10:27</reference>). Greek, "For our wrestling ('the wrestling' in which we are engaged) is not against flesh," &c. Flesh and blood foes are Satan's mere tools, the real foe lurking behind them is Satan himself, with whom our conflict is. "Wrestling" implies that it is a hand-to-hand and foot-to-foot struggle for the mastery: to wrestle successfully with Satan, we must wrestle with God in irresistible prayer like Jacob (<reference osisRef="Gen.32.24-Gen.32.29">Ge 32:24-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.12.4">Ho 12:4</reference>). The same grades of powers are specified in the case of the demons here, as in that of angels there (compare <reference osisRef="Rom.8.38">Ro 8:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.15.24">1Co 15:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.2.15">Col 2:15</reference>). The Ephesians had practiced sorcery (<reference osisRef="Acts.19.19">Ac 19:19</reference>), so that he appropriately treats of evil spirits in addressing them. The more clearly any book of Scripture, as this, treats of the economy of the kingdom of light, the more clearly does it set forth the kingdom of darkness. Hence, nowhere does the satanic kingdom come more clearly into view than in the Gospels which treat of Christ, the true Light.<div eID="gen35819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35820" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rulers of the darkness of this world--</hi>Greek, "age" or "course of the world." But the oldest manuscripts omit "of world." Translate, "Against the world rulers of this (present) darkness" (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.2">Ep 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.8">5:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.22.53">Lu 22:53</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.1.13">Col 1:13</reference>). Though they be "world rulers," they are not the ruler of the universe; and their usurped rule of the world is soon to cease, when He shall "come whose right it is" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.21.27">Eze 21:27</reference>). Two cases prove Satan not to be a mere subjective fancy: (1) Christ's temptation; (2) the entrance of demons into the swine (for these are incapable of such fancies). Satan tries to parody, or imitate in a perverted way, God's working (<reference osisRef="2Cor.11.13">2Co 11:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.11.14">14</reference>). The alteration of expression to "in heavenly places," is in order to mark the higher range of their powers than ours, they having been, up to the ascension (<reference osisRef="Rev.12.5">Re 12:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.9.10">9, 10</reference>), dwellers "in the heavenly places" (<reference osisRef="Job.1.7">Job 1:7</reference>), and being now in the regions of the air which are called the heavens. But believers have naught to fear, being "blessed with all spiritual blessings in the heavenly places" (<reference osisRef="Eph.1.3">Ep 1:3</reference>). <div eID="gen35822" type="x-p"/>

Contrast the malediction on all who love Him not (<reference osisRef="1Cor.16.22">1Co 16:22</reference>).<div eID="gen35861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35862" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in sincerity--</hi>Greek, "in incorruption," that is, not as English Version, but "with an immortal (constant) love" [Wahl]. Compare "that which is not corruptible" (<reference osisRef="1Pet.3.4">1Pe 3:4</reference>). Not a fleeting, earthly love, but a spiritual and eternal one [Alford]. Contrast <reference osisRef="Col.2.22">Col 2:22</reference>, worldly things "which perish with the using." Compare <reference osisRef="1Cor.9.25">1Co 9:25</reference>, "corruptible ... incorruptible crown."
